title: Affinity Contracts and Fidelity Boundaries: product guide and rollout plan
author: Claire Zhang
body:
Executive summary:

This document introduces the "Affinity Contract" concept and the related notion of Fidelity Boundaries. Affinity Contracts are a customer-visible contract describing how traffic will be routed, cached, and served across edge/hosted/dedicated surfaces to meet latency and cost objectives. Fidelity Boundaries define the observable guarantees for output quality under constrained capacity or cheaper execution modes (e.g., quantized variants, distilled models, or cached prefix completion).

Goals:
- Provide product definitions that let customers select predictable trade-offs (latency vs cost vs fidelity).
- Surface a simple contract model that the API, Console, and Billing can reference.
- Define requirements, telemetry, and rollout plan so engineering and GTM can deliver an initial MVP for Dedicated and Hosted in Q1 2026.

Problem statement:
Many customers need predictable behavior when inference capacity is constrained (bursting, regional outages, or deliberate cost-saving fallbacks). Past incidents and feedback highlight three recurring issues:
1) opaque fallbacks which change output quality without notifying the application;
2) difficulty mapping pricing tiers to observed fidelity;
3) lack of a migration path between hosted and Dedicated with consistent expectations.

Definitions (product terms):
- Affinity Contract: a declarative attachment that ties a tenant (or route) to a routing policy, cache affinity (local vs global), and an ordered fallback set of model variants. Example attributes: affinity_id, latency_target_ms, primary_surface, fallback_sequence, cache_scope, cost_budget_label.
- Fidelity Boundary: a named level (e.g., "gold","silver","bronze") that bundles expected distributional quality constraints: accuracy loss budget (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-specific metrics), token-level regeneration budget, and supported feature set (tool calls, streaming, function-calling).
- Consumption Unit: the billing primitive that maps tokens/embedding units to a priced SKU and can be bound to an Affinity Contract for discounting or commitment credits.

Product requirements (MVP):
1) API: create/update Affinity Contract endpoints and route binding.
   - POST /v1/affinity_contracts {name, tenant_id, latency_target_ms, fidelity_level, cache_scope, fallback_sequence, billing_label}
   - GET /v1/routes/{route_id}/affinity -> JSON contract snapshot
2) Console: UI to visualize contract, fidelity boundary definitions, and expected fallback behaviors.
3) Telemetry: per-contract telemetry exposed in Console and usage APIs: 95th token latency, fallback_rate, observed fidelity delta vs baseline, and per-token cost.
4) Billing integration: optional per-contract discounts and commit mapping; must include a reconciliation report.
5) Safety & compatibility: fidelity boundaries must declare unsupported features (e.g., no tool-calls in bronze) so SDKs can surface warnings.

Design overview (high-level):
- Runtime routing layer will annotate requests with affinity_id. The router consults the Affinity Store (config) to pick the serving variant.
- Fallback is policy-driven: either automatic ordered fallback or can be probabilistic (percentage-based route-splitting).
- Cache affinity: cache keys include affinity_id when cache_scope == "tenant-local" to avoid cross-tenant pollution.
- Observability contract: every request logs (affinity_id, selected_variant, used_cache_hit, fallback_reason) to the tracing system.

API example (contract JSON):
{
  "affinity_id": "aff-A123",
  "name": "low-latency-chat-main",
  "latency_target_ms": 150,
  "fidelity_level": "silver",
  "primary_surface": "hosted-gpu-v2",
  "fallback_sequence": ["hosted-gpu-v1-quant","dedicated-gpu-a100"],
  "cache_scope": "tenant-local",
  "billing_label": "commit-2026-q1"
}

Telemetry table (example report columns):
| column | description | example threshold |
| 95p_token_latency_ms | per-contract 95th percentile token latency | <= 200ms |
| fallback_rate_pct | percent of requests that used non-primary variant | <= 5% |
| fidelity_delta_tau | composite quality delta vs baseline (lower is better) | <= 0.03 |
| cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | observed unit cost for contract | informational |

Pricing & packaging implications:
- Offer three fidelity tiers mapped to standard SKUs: Gold (no fallbacks; higher price), Silver (fallbacks allowed with fidelity guarantees), Bronze (cost-optimized; larger fidelity boundaries).
- Introduce per-affinity commit discounts: customers who bind routes to an affinity with a monthly commit get a discounted cost_per_1k_tokens_usd and access to higher cache_sharing quotas.
- Billing edge case: when fallback to cheaper variant occurs, we bill using the actually executed variant's unit cost but record a fidelity override event for billing reconciliation.

Roadmap & milestones (target timeline):
- Q4 2025: Spec freeze, datastore schema, and API design review.
- Q1 2026: Backend runtime hooks, basic Console UI, and telemetry pipeline. Pilot with 3 customers on Hosted.
- Q2 2026: Dedicated support and billing reconciliation; initial GTM materials and pricing experiments.
- Q3 2026: Feature flags for probabilistic fallbacks and affinity-aware autoscaling.

Rollout playbook (pilot -> GA):
1) Internal canary: deploy to staging with synthetic workloads and verify telemetry and SLOs.
2) Beta customers (3–5): enable Affinity Contracts with console support and weekly syncs.
3) Open beta: invite self-serve customers to opt-in via Console with clear warnings.
4) GA: enable default availability on Hosted and Dedicated with documentation and pricing table.

Customer migration recipe (short):
1) Inventory routes: list top 10 routes by token consumption and latency.
2) Define affinity proposals: for each route, choose latency_target_ms and fidelity_level.
3) Run shadow mode for 72 hours (affinity applied to logging only).
4) Move to live, monitor fallback_rate and fidelity_delta. If fallback_rate > 10% for 48h, escalate to SRE and consider increasing capacity or relaxing latency_target_ms.

Operational & ownership notes:
- Product: owns the contract definition, Console UX, pricing mapping, and GTM materials.
- Runtime team: implements routing hooks, cache-affinity enforcement, and variant selection logic.
- Billing: owns reconciliation, invoice lines, and commit-discount logic.
- SRE: defines alert thresholds: fallback_rate_pct > 5% (P3), fidelity_delta_tau > 0.05 (P2), 95p_token_latency_ms > target*1.5 (P1).

Open questions and risks:
- Standardizing fidelity metrics across model families (instruction-following vs retrieval-augmented).
- Customer expectations when fidelity budgets are consumed mid-request.
- Pricing elasticity: will customers prefer simpler per-token discounts over routed commitments?

Appendix: example Console copy for affinity card
Title: Affinity contract: low-latency-chat-main
Subtext: Latency target 150ms · Fidelity: Silver · Primary surface: Hosted GPU · Fallbacks permitted
Buttons: Edit affinity | View telemetry | Migrate route

Next steps:
- Product to finalize fidelity boundary definitions with Applied ML team by 2026-01-30.
- Runtime to deliver proof-of-concept for per-request affinity annotation by 2026-02-15.
- Billing to prototype reconciliation report format by 2026-03-01.

Owners: Claire Zhang (product), Miguel Ortiz (runtime), Priya Desai (billing).
